additional_considerations.rationale: A distal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with painful leg paresthesias, caused by alcohol or associated nutritional deficiencies (e.g., thiamine, B vitamins); he drinks whiskey on weekends.
Myeloma or other paraproteinemias must be ruled out in a patient with peripheral neuropathy.
Uremia can cause a sensory peripheral neuropathy, including in diabetic patients.
Can be associated with peripheral neuropathy and other neurologic symptoms.
Polyarteritis nodosa, rheumatoid arthritis and other vasculitides can cause peripheral neuropathy and are detected with ESR, ANCA, RF and anti-CCP antibodies.

leakage_check.reason: The patient was told his erection problem is caused by diabetes, which points to organic (diabetic) erectile dysfunction, gold diagnosis #3. It is scripted patient content and is kept.

source_issues: patient_note_history is empty in the source file: the raw sheet's note heading is 'Patient Note' without a colon, so the parser missed it. The full note (HPI, ROS, meds, PMH, SH, FH) is present in raw_opening and was used for checking; f009 cites it as 'note'.
p007: HbA1c result '7.210' is garbled (probably OCR); the note gives 'Last HbA1c 6 months ago was 7%'. Recorded as about 7% with a flag.
e009: '6 Babinski bilaterally' - the '6' is a garbled symbol (probably a circled minus or plus); direction not stated; recorded as 'Result not documented' with a flag (x022).

Contradiction between SP notes and the note exam: the SP is told to show loss of sharp/dull, vibration and position sense in both feet (stocking distribution), but the note exam records only diminished pinprick on the plantar surfaces and intact soft touch, vibration and position sense. Both are kept (x023-x029).
p034: alcohol amount is not given; the answer trails off ('only on the weekend...').
Erectile problem duration: script 'One or 2 years' (p040); the note and gold say 2 years.

p012 asks about dizziness and confusion among hypoglycemic symptoms, and p015 about headaches, dizziness and weakness; the answers address only sweating/racing heart and foot tingling/numbness, so these items are neither confirmed nor denied by the script (the note's 'ROS: Negative except as above' is generic and was not used to create denials).
p038 ('Are you currently sexually active?') is not answered directly; the patient describes a performance problem instead.
gold_additional_diagnosis starts with a general sentence about non-diabetic neuropathy causes (not a diagnosis); 'thiamine and vitamin B' is probably truncated (e.g., B12).
Gold #3 'History of alcohol use' rests on weekend whiskey with no stated amount.
annotator_notes: Per a later policy update (which overrides the GUIDE.md Babinski example wording), env findings carry no review commentary: an undirected Babinski is recorded as 'Result not documented' and the reason is in the record's flags.
The chief complaint is a visit reason (diabetes checkup), used as the opening fact as written.

Diabetes and its management (insulin, monitoring, HbA1c, eye and foot care) are coded history_and_exposures; the symptoms elicited (sweating/racing-heart episodes, foot numbness/tingling, erectile problem) are coded symptoms.
The sweating/racing-heart episodes are described in the patient's words without the label 'hypoglycemia' to avoid naming the rank-1 diagnosis.
'I don't even wake up with erections anymore' is coded as a present symptom (loss of morning erections), per guide rule 2.
p003 (no medication side effects) is recorded literally even though the sweating episodes may be insulin-related.
f053 combines 'Do you smoke? Did you ever smoke in the past?' - 'No' as a never-smoker.
